svg.title: Hyperscale Agent Meta Harness architecture on AWS
svg.desc: Left to right: the ham terminal app on a Mac signs a request to Amazon API Gateway (1, 2). AWS Lambda control-api checks it and starts an AWS Step Functions run (3, 4). The run-session Lambda starts one Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime microVM per run, inside a VPC private subnet (5). In the microVM agentd drives Cline, the harness that runs today; other harnesses (OpenCode, Pi, etc.) are drawn as a design behind an engine adapter. Cline calls Amazon Bedrock models. Packages come from AWS CodeArtifact through a loopback proxy, and AWS Network Firewall drops every host that is not on the allowlist (6). After Cline stops, Lambda functions validate the work, open an AWS CodeCommit pull request and write a zip to Amazon S3, which ham pulls (7). IAM roles, AWS STS short-lived credentials, Amazon ECR images and Amazon CloudWatch logs serve every step (8).
svg.text: Region us-east-1: stage direct (resources named hamh-direct-*)
The Cline harness on the full AWS stack
Other harnesses (OpenCode, Pi, etc.) attach through
an engine adapter, which is a design.
